title: Lesson 2: Comparison Operators
lessonSummary: Equal, smaller, greater – you know the six comparison operators and never mix up = and ==!

tasks.instruction: Run this example: it compares heights and checks the hay.
tasks.codeTemplate:
height = 160
print(f"Height at withers: {height} cm")
print(f"{height} < 165: {height < 165}")
print(f"{height} <= 160: {height <= 160}")
print(f"{height} > 150: {height > 150}")
print(f"{height} >= 160: {height >= 160}")

hay = 25
need = 20
if hay > need:
    print(f"🌾 Enough hay! Leftover: {hay - need} kg")

tasks.instruction: age = 8 is already there. Use an if with == to print exactly: Correct: The horse is 8 years old
tasks.codeTemplate:
age = 8
# 🎯 Your solution here:

validation.expected: Correct: The horse is 8 years old

tasks.instruction: height = 160 is already there. Use an f-string with a comparison inside the braces to print exactly: 160 > 170: False

title: Lesson 5: Logical Operators – and, or, not
lessonSummary: and, or, not – you can combine several conditions into one decision!

tasks.instruction: Run this example: and, or and not in action.
tasks.codeTemplate:
has_saddle = True
has_helmet = True
if has_saddle and has_helmet:
    print("🐎🪖 You are ready to ride!")

has_bridle = False
has_halter = True
if has_bridle or has_halter:
    print("🐴 You can lead the horse!")

is_sick = False
if not is_sick:
    print("💪 The horse is healthy and ready to work!")
